corrections: Removed environment-independent QPS, latency and pipeline speedup claims; performance must be benchmarked with the target workload.
Qualified the command execution model: individual commands have an atomic execution boundary, but Redis is not universally single-threaded and multi-command workflows need transactions or scripts.
Corrected Pipeline buffering and atomicity wording: Pipeline has no EXEC and does not reduce all work to exactly one RTT.
Updated persistence for Redis 7 multi-part AOF, removed fixed recovery-time promises, and separated durability from high availability and backups.
Qualified LRU/LFU implementation constants and removed simulated accuracy percentages and fixed per-key memory claims.

Corrected Stream semantics: Entry IDs are not consumer offsets, XACK does not delete entries or prevent duplicates, trimming can race with pending delivery, and XAUTOCLAIM is available from Redis 6.2.
Qualified Cluster heartbeat timing and manual failover; asynchronous replication does not provide an absolute zero-data-loss guarantee.
Strengthened distributed-lock boundaries with TTL expiry, failover, wall-clock and fencing-token requirements.
Removed fixed Pub/Sub/Stream/MQ latency comparisons and clarified that delivery and capacity depend on deployment and consumer behavior.

relationSuggestions.reason: Pipeline batches independent Redis data-type commands to amortize network round trips without changing their semantics.
Redis eviction implements approximate LRU/LFU using object metadata, sampling and a candidate pool.
Persistence, replication and Cluster failover cover different durability and availability failure modes.
Pub/Sub is transient at-most-once delivery, while Streams retain entries and track consumer-group pending state.
A Redis lock TTL or Redlock result alone cannot prevent a stale holder from writing to downstream resources.

openspec.action: No OpenSpec structure was introduced because this repository has no openspec convention.
